solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pub in torrid island capital

indicators.note: the pub word is placed inside the word for torrid

parts.note: torrid means very hot
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A drinker recalls a pub in a sweltering island capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobart is the capital city of Tasmania, an island state of Australia.

clue.text: Hamlet, I suspect, receives a communication sealed with venom?

indicators.note: the scrambled letters take in, receive, the a
suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hamlet suspects he has been sent a poisonous letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hate mail is abusive correspondence, figuratively full of venom rather than love.

clue.text: Country separating couple, not wanting a loving relationship between men

indicators.note: the country sits between letters of the couple word, separating them
not wanting means lacking, so the a is dropped

parts.note: a brace is a couple, a pair
Oman is a country in Arabia

explanation.surface: A nation keeping two lovers apart, disapproving of a gay relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couple' is a pair of lovers in the surface but a brace (as of pheasants) in the wordplay; 'not wanting a' drops its A before 'separating' splits it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bromance is a close, affectionate but non-sexual friendship between two men.

clue.text: Horse galloped around ring

indicators.note: the running word goes around the ring letter

parts.note: galloped means ran
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A horse galloped around a racing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A roan is a horse with a coat of mixed white and coloured hairs.

clue.text: Arrest prophet, revolutionary African

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns right round, so the two pieces before it are read backwards

parts.note: to nail someone is to arrest them
Amos is an Old Testament prophet

explanation.surface: A news story: police arrest a revolutionary prophet in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns NAILAMOS round as a whole, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Somalian is a person from Somalia, a country in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Narrowly ahead, staff on boat successfully outwitting opponents

indicators.note: in a down clue the staff piece sits on top of the boat piece

parts.note: one up, as in a game, is a narrow lead
to man something is to staff it
a ship is a boat

explanation.surface: A sailing crew edges ahead in a race against rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: The art of gaining an advantage over others, always staying a step ahead of rivals.

clue.text: Top statistics for book

indicators.note: to top is to cut off the head, the first letter, in a down clue

parts.note: facts and figures, statistics

explanation.surface: A book bursting with the best statistics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective meaning best but is a verb, beheading.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts of the Apostles is a book of the New Testament.

clue.text: Eventually, I'm here?

definitions.meaning: at some later point, after a while
what a punctual arrival might announce: I'm here, not late

explanation.surface: A latecomer finally turns up, wondering if they made it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means eventually and also punctual, not late for something.

clue.text: Country never welcoming Russians, primarily

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: no way means never

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A country refusing to welcome Russians, in a political headline.
explanation.definitionFit: Norway is a Scandinavian country bordering Russia in the far north.

clue.text: Daughter has a shoe the wrong way round — never mind

indicators.note: facing the wrong way round means the pieces before it are read from the end

parts.note: a boot is a kind of shoe

explanation.surface: A parent shrugs off a daughter wearing her shoe on the wrong foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way round' turns DABOOT backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive idioms meaning that a disappointment cannot be helped.

clue.text: One with a will to try a hill

parts.note: to test is to try something out
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone determined sets out to attempt a hill climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One with a will' reads as a determined person; it means someone who has made a legal will.
explanation.definitionFit: A testator is the person who makes a will, leaving property after death.

clue.text: Swimmers grabbing everyone fit to climb gymnastic equipment

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing and holding inside

parts.note: parrs are young salmon, swimmers
all means everyone

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing goes upward, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: able means fit, capable

explanation.surface: Swimmers grab everyone fit enough to climb some gym equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: Parr are young salmon, a crossword staple for 'swimmers'; 'to climb' reverses the fit word upward in this down clue, giving ELBA.
explanation.definitionFit: Parallel bars are an apparatus in men's artistic gymnastics.

clue.text: Average is tight

definitions.meaning: a statistical average, the arithmetic middle value

explanation.surface: A shopper's verdict: being average means being tight-fisted.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses hold: the arithmetic average and the miserly, stingy sense.

clue.text: Tinker reported in US city

indicators.note: something reported is spoken, so the word is taken by how it is said

parts.note: to tinker with something is to tamper with it

explanation.surface: A news item about a meddler in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the meddling word ends in the same sound as the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa is a city on the Gulf coast of Florida.

clue.text: Covers torn off, tool returned book

indicators.note: sent back the way it came, so the trimmed word is read backwards
the covers of a word are its outer letters, here stripped away

parts.note: a hammer is a tool

explanation.surface: A damaged library book comes back with its covers ripped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covers torn off' leaves AMME, and 'returned' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is Jane Austen's 1815 novel, so it is a book by title.

clue.text: Blow — or heroin?

definitions.meaning: street slang for the drug heroin

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses hold: a sharp slap and a slang name for heroin.

clue.text: Raw fish

definitions.meaning: a small freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.definitionFit: A bleak is a small river fish, and bleak weather is cold and raw.

clue.text: Story on wages not entirely without equal

indicators.note: in an across clue the story piece is placed on, that is after, the wages piece
not entirely means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: wages are income
a parable is a story with a moral

explanation.surface: A tale about pay that is only partly unrivalled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incomparable has no equal and cannot be matched by anything else.

clue.text: Centaurs translated old language

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A text about centaurs rendered from an ancient tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Etruscan was the language of ancient Etruria in Italy, long extinct.

clue.text: Garden frame, where rotten pear lies

indicators.note: rotten means decayed, broken down, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trellis in the garden beneath which a rotten pear lies.
explanation.definitionFit: An espalier is a trellis on which fruit trees are trained flat.

clue.text: Book is about a retro group east of Greater Manchester town

indicators.note: in an across clue east of means placed to the right of, after the town

parts.note: Eccles is a town in Greater Manchester, famous for its cakes

indicators.note: the word is goes about, around, the letter a
retro means going backwards, so the group word is read from the end

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: A book about a retro band from somewhere east of a Manchester town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the clue's own 'is' round A, giving IAS; 'retro' reverses the group word. Eccles is known for its currant-filled Eccles cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecclesiastes is a book of the Old Testament, traditionally attributed to Solomon.

clue.text: Force juice from fruit

definitions.meaning: to cram or press, as in ... into a bag
a soft drink made from fruit concentrate

explanation.surface: Pressing a fruit hard to extract its juice.
explanation.definitionFit: To squash is to force or crush, and squash is a British fruit cordial.

clue.text: Going straight, one having lost head admitted to fraud

indicators.note: admitted to means let into, so the piece goes inside

parts.note: a liar is a fraud

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before its first letter goes

explanation.surface: A reformed fraudster going straight, having confessed after losing his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going straight' suggests reform from crime; it means in a line.
explanation.definitionFit: Linear means arranged in or moving along a straight line.

clue.text: Small amount of dough, something to chew on

definitions.meaning: dough is slang for money, and one pound is a modest sum

explanation.definitionFit: It is British slang for one pound sterling and also a lump of tobacco for chewing.

clue.text: Bent, right around left

indicators.note: the word for right goes around the letter for left

parts.note: fair means right, just

explanation.surface: A political label: someone of the right bending round to the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' looks like crooked, but means a natural aptitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent is a natural talent or inclination, as is a flair for something.

clue.text: First glimpse of pussy, I'm not sure a cougar

indicators.note: the first glimpse of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: um is the hesitant noise of someone unsure

explanation.surface: Catching sight of a cat, someone wonders whether it is a big wild one.
explanation.definitionFit: The cougar and the puma are the same big American wild cat.

clue.text: Small glass container, nasty by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it signals a word spoken that sounds like another

parts.note: vile means nasty

explanation.surface: A small glass jar holding something that sounds unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A vial is a small glass bottle for medicine or liquids.

clue.text: Island into cruciverbalism

indicators.note: into here signals letters tucked inside the long word

explanation.surface: An island that has got into cruciverbalism, the hobby of crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian island.

clue.text: US army came in, not my bombs!

indicators.note: the letters bomb, explode into a new order, once the my is taken out

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged together with my

explanation.surface: A civilian's plea as foreign troops arrive: those explosives are not mine!
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters of 'my' from 'army came in' ('not my'), and 'bombs' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: US used as an adjective means belonging to the United States, as in US army.

clue.text: Coda and note, both short, in slow movements

indicators.note: each of the two words loses its last letter

parts.note: a coda is a tail-piece, the tail of a work
a chit is a short note

explanation.surface: A musician describes a coda and note, both clipped, within slow movements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both short' cuts the last letter from TAIL and CHIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tai chi is a Chinese martial art practised as a series of slow, flowing exercises.

clue.text: Safe house's opening, short of members?

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: limbs are members, so lacking arms means armless

explanation.surface: A safe house's entrance, with too few members to run it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'members' means limbs here, not people in a club.
explanation.definitionFit: Something harmless poses no danger, so it is safe.

clue.text: Starter of duck with private meal

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter

parts.note: inner thoughts are private ones

explanation.surface: A duck starter served at a private meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' hints at a course, but takes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinner is the main meal of the day, eaten in the evening.
